assertion.rationale: F17 (Task 19): infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep now adds one Microsoft.Insights/actionGroups (email receiver, the same sponsor address scripts/bootstrap/03-budget.ps1 already notifies) and two Microsoft.Insights/scheduledQueryRules against the Log Analytics workspace F9 routes diagnostics to -- a Key Vault AuditEvent denied-result spike (httpStatusCode_d >= 300 in the AzureDiagnostics table, the destination F9's diagnostic settings use by default) and an Azure SQL failed-login spike (SQLSecurityAuditEvents, succeeded_s == "false"). Both map directly to the access-pattern findings this branch closed (F1, F2, F3) generalised to the estate's two real credential-and-data surfaces -- Key Vault (the Direct Line secret, mcp-auth-token) and Azure SQL (Entra-only auth, F13's workload grants). A third rule for Container Apps restart counts (the brief's own suggestion) was deliberately dropped: the individual container app resources a meaningful restart metric would attach to do not exist at L6 -- they deploy at L7 -- so a metricAlert cannot be authored here without an app resource id this template never sees, and no log-based proxy at the environment scope has a Microsoft-documented contract precise enough to write with confidence absent a live workspace. A cost/usage-spike rule was also deliberately not duplicated: Task 17/F15 already added Forecasted budget notifications for that gap. Both rules evaluate every 15 minutes, the cheapest scheduled-query-rule frequency tier, keeping combined cost on the order of a dollar or two per month against the $200/30-day credit. SI-4 is tailored out of NIST SP 800-171 but system monitoring for indicators of compromise is exactly what CMMC assessors probe; F17 was this control's sole contributor, and with F17 closed this control closes outright. Checked: no other finding in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md cites SI-4.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. A regression here -- the action group or either scheduledQueryRule removed from platform/main.bicep without replacement, or both rules' queries stop matching the AzureDiagnostics schema F9's diagnostic settings actually populate -- would reopen it.
